title: The limit points of the strong law of large numbers under the sub-linear expectations
abstract: Let $\{X_n;n\ge 1\}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables relative to a regular sub-linear expectation $(Ω,\mathscr{H},\widehat{\mathbb E})$ with upper mean $\overlineμ$, lower mean $\underlineμ$, and finite Choquet expectation or $\lim_{c\to\infty} \widehat{\mathbb E}[(|X_1|-c)^+]=0$. Then for any Borel-measurable function $\varphi(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$ on $\mathbb R^d$ or continuous function $\varphi(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ on $\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$, $\sum_{i=1}^nX_i/n$ converges to $\underlineμ\wedge \varphi(X_1,X_2,\ldots)\wedge \overlineμ$ with upper capacity $1$. The set of limit points of $\sum_{i=1}^nX_i/n$ is the whole mean interval $[\underlineμ,\overlineμ]$ with upper capacity $1$, as is any random subset of the mean interval whose boundaries are continuous functions or finite-dimensional Borel-measurable functions of $(X_1, X_2, \ldots)$, also with upper capacity $1$.
